items.text: It is important torememberthat the rubbingaction doesnotproduce or create charge.lt simply separates charge-that is,it transfers some electrons from one object toanother.

items.text: We canshowhowinsulatingmaterialscanbe chargedby friction using anunchargedplasticrod and anuncharged cloth.Firstwe have to check they arenotalreadycharged.We can do thisbyplacing therod and the cloth in tum,close tosomevery small piecesofpaper.lf the cloth or the rod ischarged,some of the paperwill be attracted.lf they are uncharged there willbenoattraction (see page 88).Now werub therod and the cloth togetherfora fewseconds and then retest them.Because they are made from different insulating materials theywill be charged.

items.text: Ifwerepeat this experiment using objects that arenotinsulators,or are madefrom the same material,theywill not attract the smallpieces of paper.That is,theyremain uncharged.
